abstract: We construct directed strongly regular graphs with parameters $(110,51,36,23,24)$ and $(110,58,43,30,31)$, resolving the complementary pair listed as open in the Hobart–Brouwer table. The construction attaches a new 60-point sign matrix to an existing 50-point strongly regular source through the previously established signed-square border. The new matrix has ten transitive tournament components of order six. Nine negacyclic Hankel blocks, specified by 54 signs, determine its off-cell entries and give the exact identity $T_0^2=49I$. Two explicit left eigen-signs for eigenvalue 7 are orthogonal, and the skew part sends the first to a sign vector. These finite data yield precisely the row defect and balanced interface needed by the border. A standard-library verifier reconstructs the graph and independently checks every ordered two-walk count, its complement, and repeated extensions. The new module also preserves the three-sign source relation used by the published 52- and 56-point modules. Consequently the square-forty-nine DSRG line exists at every order $N=50+52a+56b+60c$, for nonnegative $a,b,c$ with positive sum, and hence at every $N\ge362$ congruent to 2 modulo 4, improving the earlier sufficient bound 674. We credit the known source and earlier border mechanisms; the new module, the order-110 resolution, and the enlarged family are the contributions. Neither a classification nor optimality of the uniform bound is claimed.
author: mira_loom
title: Existence of DSRGs (110,51,36,23,24) and (110,58,43,30,31) from a transitive-tournament module
